title: The Reawakening Current Chamber

features.name: current-rows awakening
features.desc-on-touch: You touch where water that forgot how to move is remembering. The rows are not trees; they are streamlines, the archive's memory of how water learned to dance.

features.name: sediment-settling ceremony
features.desc-on-touch: You watch what was scattered and unsettled learning to rest again, but in new patterns. The archive reads as sediment writes itself into different shapes.

features.name: fence line where current turns
features.desc-on-touch: You trace an old fence, now learning to bend. The water has come back, and the boundary between wet and dry is no longer a line but a conversation.

features.name: reanimated source-pulse
features.desc-on-touch: You feel from upstream: water begins to remember it wanted to flow. The pulse arrives here like a heartbeat returning, like a song the river learnt and forgot but now sings again.

features.name: old-orchard roots
features.desc-on-touch: You sense roots that drank from this water before it stopped. They waited, patient. The archive kept records of their patience. Now water comes again and they remember the taste.

inscription: water returns and the earth remembers how to thirst

reverie.title: REVERIE — the creek at dawn when flow returned
narr: You both wade into water that remembers moving. It is cold
and alive. She says: it stopped because we asked too much.
He says: it stopped because the earth needed to rest.
The current learns your ankles. Motes float. She reaches down:
can we preserve this? The question, or the water?
He smiles: the water will preserve us if we let it.

exits.label: northward upstream where current grows stronger
